ai.description: *Cnemaspis heteropholis* reaches 45 mm SVL. It is brown with a pale vertebral stripe and dark lateral spots. Distinctive features include heterogeneous dorsal scales and a lack of precloacal pores.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Cnemaspis heteropholis* is best distinguished by the presence of large, scattered, spine-like tubercles on its flanks, which are absent in most other Indian congeners.
ai.habitat: *Cnemaspis heteropholis* inhabits the moist deciduous and evergreen forests of the Western Ghats, typically found on tree trunks at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Gund Day Gecko is strictly nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates on rock surfaces while remaining hidden in crevices during the day.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Cnemaspis heteropholis* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two eggs. Breeding occurs during the monsoon season, typically between June and September.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Cnemaspis heteropholis* is endemic to the Western Ghats of Karnataka, India, typically found in moist deciduous forests at elevations between 600 and 1,000 meters.
